relevance_note: Case report of a child with a TNFAIP3 variant plus a literature table of 15 pediatric patients: 'Whole exome sequencing revealed a heterozygous mutation in the affected TNFAIP3 gene'.
method_note: Read the paper fully by hand; a short Python script in the scratch directory transcribed Table 3 (15 literature patients, patients as rows) into rows using contiguous row-prefix spans, and its output was checked against the table. Labels: the case-report child is 'patient' (the paper's 'first witness' is a role word); Table 3 rows use 'Table 3 #<n>' from the bare index number in the 'Patients' column, whose bracketed number is the reference, copied into source_reference_in_review. Table 3 legend defines 'N, no', so N cells are recorded as excluded with the legend quoted; narrower columns (recurrent oral/genital ulcers, rash, arthritis, GI ulcers) with N do not exclude the broader checklist items, which stay not reported. '—'/'−' cells and 'Without elaborating' are not reported. Age (y) in Table 3 is age at diagnosis per the table notes. Relatives: father (carries the variant per the text), mother (sequenced in Figure 1) and the child's grandparents ('tested negative'; number not stated, recorded as two rows) are included as tested relatives; no variant rows for those who tested negative. The grandparents are not said to be paternal, so the father's inheritance and parental testing are left not reported. Father's variant type/pathogenicity left not reported (stated for the proband's variant only). The patient's ages: 3 years and 6 months at admission; he was followed up 1 month and 10 months later, so age at last evaluation, onset and diagnosis are not reported. Normal examinations ('The rest of the cardiopulmonary, abdominal, joint, and neurological examination showed no significant abnormality', bone marrow smear normal, CSF negative) are recorded as the whole examination being abnormal = excluded, nothing more specific. Lab abnormalities were recorded only where the text names them or the table prints Normal/Negative/Weakly positive; raw numeric values were not judged against reference ranges myself. 'pendulous ulcers' recorded verbatim; not mapped to genital ulcers. Contradictions: (1) the Discussion says 'no special abnormalities in rheumatologic immune indicators on comprehensive examination', while it also states abnormalities in antinuclear antibodies and ANCA (ANA 33.3, P-ANCA weakly positive in Table 1); both rows emitted and the autoantibodies checklist item set to not reported. (2) Text says 'high IgE and IgA on admission' but Table 1 IgA 1.47 g/L lies within the printed range 1.45–3.45; the text statement was recorded. (3) Text says IL-10 was elevated, but Table 1 has no IL-10 value. Not given rows: the Discussion's ref (9) child (autologous transplant, relapse) has no sex, age, variant or feature beyond treatment course; refs (12, 19) EBV co-infection is a group statement. The Discussion's ref (2) patient (fluctuating autoantibodies) is recorded as its own row and not merged with Table 3 #1/#2 (also ref 2). The patient's Table 2 'Alpha thalassemia gene SEA deletion' is recorded as a variant in another gene. Checklist mapping: Table 3 'Autoimmune thyroid disorder' mapped to autoimmune thyroiditis observed; 'Hypothyroidism', 'hepatitis' and 'cytopenias' (autoimmune not stated) left not reported in the checklist; 'Insulin-dependent diabetes' mapped to type 1 diabetes; 'Pericardial effusion' to serositis; 'small vessel CNS vasculitis' to CNS involvement and vasculitis.
